findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of 15 high-quality randomized controlled trials reported that red yeast rice lowered LDL cholesterol by 1.02 mmol/L versus placebo — a 15-25% reduction within 6-8 weeks — with LDL-lowering not different from statin therapy in comparative trials.
findings.limitations: red yeast rice's active monacolin K is chemically identical to lovastatin; commercial products vary widely in monacolin content

findings.finding_summary: Across the included trials, the incidence of liver and kidney injury was 0-5% and not different between red yeast rice and control groups.
findings.limitations: the authors note adverse-event design and reporting were insufficient in most studies to make a firm safety judgment

findings.finding_summary: This updated meta-analysis of 20 trials (970 participants) reported mean reductions of 5.1 mmHg systolic and 2.5 mmHg diastolic blood pressure versus placebo, with garlic supplements highly tolerated.
findings.limitations: modest absolute effect; other systematic reviews judge the overall evidence not strong and call for a longer, well-powered trial

findings.endpoint: major cardiovascular events in statin-treated patients with elevated triglycerides (REDUCE-IT)
findings.population: statin-treated adults with triglycerides 135-500 mg/dL and cardiovascular disease or diabetes (n=8,179)
findings.finding_summary: In the REDUCE-IT trial, 4 g/day icosapent ethyl (purified EPA) reduced the primary composite endpoint (cardiovascular death, MI, stroke, revascularization, unstable angina) to 17.2% versus 22.0% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.75, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.83).
findings.limitations: a prescription-grade purified EPA ester at 4 g/day in a high-risk statin-treated population — results do not generalize to over-the-counter fish-oil supplements

findings.endpoint: all-cause mortality and cardiovascular events (supplemental EPA+DHA)
findings.population: adults with and without cardiovascular disease (86 trials, 162,796 participants)
findings.finding_summary: This Cochrane review (86 trials, 162,796 participants) found high-certainty evidence that increasing EPA and DHA has little or no effect on deaths and cardiovascular events, and moderate-certainty evidence of little or no difference in cardiovascular death, stroke, or arrhythmia.
findings.limitations: low-certainty evidence suggested a possible slight reduction in coronary death and coronary events; triglyceride lowering is established

findings.endpoint: major adverse cardiovascular events in chronic heart failure (Q-SYMBIO)
findings.population: adults with moderate-to-severe chronic heart failure (n=420, 17 centers)
findings.finding_summary: In the Q-SYMBIO randomized double-blind trial, CoQ10 added to standard therapy halved major adverse cardiovascular events at week 106 (15% versus 26%, hazard ratio 0.50, p=0.003).
findings.limitations: 420 patients is small for a mortality-bearing endpoint; a confirmatory large trial has not been completed

findings.endpoint: cardiovascular and all-cause mortality in chronic heart failure
findings.population: adults with moderate-to-severe chronic heart failure (n=420)
findings.finding_summary: The same trial reported reduced cardiovascular mortality (18 versus 34 deaths, hazard ratio 0.51, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.92) and all-cause mortality (21 versus 39, hazard ratio 0.51, 95% CI 0.30 to 0.89) with CoQ10 versus placebo.
findings.limitations: same small-trial caveat as the MACE row; mortality was a secondary endpoint

findings.endpoint: maximal workload and symptoms in chronic heart failure
findings.population: patients with NYHA class I-III chronic heart failure (8 trials, 632 patients)
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of eight randomized trials (632 patients) found hawthorn extract as an adjunct to standard therapy improved maximal workload versus placebo (weighted mean difference 7 W, 95% CI 3 to 11 W), with significant improvement in dyspnea and fatigue.
findings.limitations: adjunctive use in older trials with standardized extracts; no mortality or event outcomes

findings.population: adults in randomized placebo-controlled trials across a continuous dose range
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis found clear, comparable dose-response LDL-cholesterol reductions for plant sterols and stanols at intakes up to 3 g/day, with maximal reductions of about 8.4% for plant sterol esters versus 17.1% for plant stanol esters.
findings.limitations: LDL is a surrogate endpoint — no cardiovascular outcome trials exist for plant sterol/stanol esters

findings.population: adults in randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials (34 trials, 2,028 participants)
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of 34 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials (2,028 participants) found magnesium supplementation at a median 368 mg/day for a median 3 months reduced systolic blood pressure by 2.00 mmHg and diastolic by 1.78 mmHg.
findings.limitations: small average effect at the population level; relevance greatest where baseline magnesium status is low
